title: Tissue Processing and RNA Extraction for Multi-Omic Analyses of Human Samples
author: Matthew R. Sapio
materials: Transport tube back to "RNAse free" bench.
Remove Bioanalyzer reagents and DNase buffer from 4 °C fridge and DNase from -20 °C freezer.
Schedule of activities for study procedures.
These steps are adapted from the PureLink‱ RNA Mini Kit (Catalog numbers: 12183018A, 12183025, Thermo Fisher Scientific).
Transport tube back to "RNAse free" bench.

steps.title: Pre-operative and Peri-operative Coordination
steps.instruction: Coordinate surgical timing and patient assessments.

substeps.instruction: Review medical history and physical exam.
Administer Brief Pain Inventory (BPI) and McGill-short form (sf-MPQ) questionnaires prior to surgery.
Document initial surgical incision time and organize subsequent time point samples.
Obtain tissue samples at 0, 1, 2, 4, and 6 hours, and at closure if surgery lasts ≥8 hours.
Administer BPI and sf-MPQ questionnaires on Post-Operative Day 1 and Day 2.

steps.title: Surgical Tissue Collection
steps.instruction: Collect and subdivide tissue samples according to specific analysis requirements.

substeps.instruction: Obtain samples from lateral aspects of the incision line (not covered by self-retaining retractors) using surgical scissors or scalpel.
Measure each sample using a sterile 6-inch ruler.
Collect an initial sample (~1 x 2 x 2 mm) at 0 hour in a sterile container with sterile water for pathology identification.
Subdivide the main sample (24 mm) into three equal pieces of approximately 8 mm each:
RNA-Seq: Place 8 mm piece in RNA later; store overnight (10-18 hours) at 2-8°C, then freeze at -80°C.
Mass Spectrometry: Place 8 mm piece in 1.5 mL microtube; freeze on dry ice and store at -80°C.

Histology: Place 8 mm piece (preferably the section with more subcutaneous fat) in 10% formalin; store overnight (10-18 hours) at 2-8°C, then switch to 1% paraformaldehyde or 2.5% formalin for paraffin embedding.

steps.title: Prepare RNAse-Free Workspace
steps.instruction: Establish a sterile environment to prevent RNA degradation.

substeps.instruction: Set centrifuge to 4 °C.
Prepare two temperature-stable buckets with dry ice and wet ice; place frozen samples on dry ice.
Cover bench top with aluminum foil secured by lab tape.
Decontaminate the area by spraying RNAse Zap and wiping clean with Milliq purified RNAse free water and a Kimwipe.
Spray gloved hands, bench, and tube holders with RNAse Zap.

steps.title: Tissue Homogenization
steps.instruction: Break down the tissue sample for RNA extraction.

substeps.instruction: Place tissues on Kimwipe paper and carefully remove RNA later solution.
Place tissue into a 14 ml round bottom PCR clean homogenization tube.
Add 1 mL of Qiazol to the tube.
Homogenize using a rotor stator homogenizer with a 10 mm saw-toothed probe until minimal pieces remain (liquid with few small chunks).
Transfer the solution to a 15 mL conical centrifuge tube (or 2 mL tube if volume allows).

steps.title: Phase Separation
steps.instruction: Separate the RNA-containing aqueous phase from proteins and lipids.

substeps.instruction: In a chemical fume hood, add 200 µL of chloroform to the homogenate.
Manually mix for 15 seconds and let sit for 2–3 minutes until two layers form.
Centrifuge at 12,000 g for 15 minutes at 4 °C (ensure g-force is used, not RPM).
Set centrifuge to 22°C after this step.

steps.title: RNA Binding and Washing
steps.instruction: Isolate RNA using a spin column.

substeps.instruction: Carefully pipette 400 µL of clear supernatant into a new microcentrifuge tube.
Add an approximately equal volume of 70% ethanol and vortex for 5 seconds.
Transfer ≤ 700 µL to a pink RNA extraction mini spin column (use a second flowthrough if volume exceeds 700 µL).
Centrifuge at 8,000 g for 22 seconds and decant flow-through.
Add 350 µL Wash Buffer 1, close lid, and centrifuge for 22 seconds at 12,000 g; discard flow-through.

steps.title: On-Column DNase Digestion
steps.instruction: Remove contaminating DNA from the RNA sample.

substeps.instruction: Prepare DNase mix in a separate tube: 10 µL DNase solution, 8 μL 10xDNase buffer, and 62 µL RNase free water.
Add 80 µL of the incubated DNase mix directly to the spin column, ensuring the membrane is covered and not touched by the pipette tip.

steps.title: Final RNA Purification and Elution
steps.instruction: Wash the RNA and elute the final product.

substeps.instruction: Add 500 µL Wash Buffer 2 (with ethanol), centrifuge at 12,000 g for 20 seconds, and discard flow-through.
Add 350 µL Wash Buffer 1 (up to 700 µL for better QC), centrifuge at 12,000 g for 20 seconds with the lid open to dry the membrane.
Repeat the Wash Buffer 1 step if necessary.
Centrifuge the spin column at 12,000 g for 2 minutes with the lid open to fully dry the membrane.
Place the column in a new 1.5 mL RNAse-free collection tube.
Add 50 µL RNase-free water directly to the column, close lid, and centrifuge for 2 minutes at 12,000 g.

steps.title: Sample Storage
steps.instruction: Store the extracted RNA for future use.

substeps.instruction: Label the samples and store at -80 °C.

description: Graphic overview of timepoints for skin collection. Location of intraoperative tissue sampling. Samples were collected adjacent to one another to maintain a bordering edge with the initial incision. Care was taken to avoid areas of retractor contact, or other unrelated trauma, when possible.
